issue.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies

arms.better: The run reached the correct stream flush code quickly and recovered from both a guessed `.js` test-helper path and a missing-evidence submission. However, the transcript repeats searches and rereads `test/stream.ts` many times, and `tm stats --json` reports 1,107,519 tokens despite a 153-second run. A user would also have to interpret an initially failed ticket submission followed by `Saved a result` and a submitted state; finish with one clear summary of changed files, the checks actually run, and their results, and avoid repeatedly loading the same test file after locating the relevant case.

OpenCode found the precise flush guard and the stream test quickly, gave a scoped plan, and corrected its first regression fixture after observing that `new Response(null)` does not exercise the empty readable-stream path. It reported its own 18 stream tests, XO, and diff check accurately. The independent merge-test verification still failed: the full test command hits an XO error in untouched `test/http-error.ts`, and the broader targeted AVA invocation lacks Firefox/WebKit browser installations. Include the independent verification result in any final summary so the locally passing focused test is not mistaken for the protocol's hidden-test pass.

verification.command: pnpm test; pnpm exec ava test/browser.ts test/stream.ts
verification.details: pnpm test exits 1 at XO for an unrelated existing error in test/http-error.ts:218 (@typescript-eslint/no-meaningless-void-operator). The targeted AVA run exits 1: the hidden empty-response browser test fails in Chromium because no completion callback was recorded, and Firefox/WebKit tests cannot launch because their Playwright browsers are unavailable. The hidden test in test/stream.ts passes for both arms. Both test files were overwritten from merge SHA 99644d0169138eb0c42718f06862061288f05a96 before verification.
